question.problem: An infectious flu virus is spreading through a school. The probability of a randomly selected student having the flu next week is $0.2.$ If a class has $23$ students, what is the standard deviation of the number of students having the flu next week? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be the number of students having the flu next week.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=23$ students in the class

- the probability of selecting a student having the flu next week is $0.2$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(23,0.2).$ 

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the number of students having the flu next week is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{(23)(0.2)(1-0.2)} \\  & =\sqrt{(23)(0.2)(0.8)} \\  & =\sqrt{3.68} \\  & ≈1.918\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
